The synthetic data contract of one table

Source: R/r6_SyntheticTable.R
SyntheticTable.Rd

A SyntheticTable holds the contract of one table and its fixed synthetic datasets. Every data.table that a SyntheticTable returns passed $validate().

A generator is a function(profile, n, seed, world) that returns a data.table. generator = NULL uses simulate_from_profile() on profile, or on profile_schema() of field_types and keys when profile is NULL. n = NULL means the generator's own size. A generator MAY then choose its row count, for example a complete grid of series and weeks. simulate_from_profile() gives 1000 rows for n = NULL.

$validate(d, world) checks d in this order, and stops at the first check that fails. The error names the check.

  1. columns: d is a data.table, and its column names and order equal names(field_types).

  2. types: each column has the R type of its field type. These are TEXT character, INTEGER integer, DOUBLE double, BOOLEAN logical, DATE Date and DATETIME POSIXct.

  3. keys: no two rows have the same values of keys.

  4. validator_field_contents: validator_field_contents(d) is TRUE.

  5. invariant '<name>': each invariant returns TRUE. A character return is the error message.

An invariant is a function(d) or a function(d, world). The class calls an invariant with two or more formal arguments as f(d, world), and any other invariant as f(d). $random(), $dataset() and $add_dataset() give the invariants their world.

The directory dir holds the datasets of the table:

  • datasets.yaml: one entry for each recipe, with name, kind, n, seed, description, overrides, world_md5, rows and md5. n is empty for n = NULL. world_md5 is absent for world = NULL. rows is the row count of the data.

  • handmade/<name>.csv: one handmade dataset. Each column is read as text and converted to its field type. An empty cell is NA.

  • profile.yaml: optional. synthetic_table_from_dir() reads it. $new() does not read it.

A dataset name is lower snake case. The name default is the generator output at seed = 1 and n = 1000 or n = NULL.

The md5 of a recipe comes from tools::md5sum() of the data that data.table::fwrite() writes with eol = "\n". The columns are in field_types order, the rows are sorted by every column, dates are ISO 8601 and NA is empty.

The md5 of a world comes from tools::md5sum() of the text that yaml::as.yaml() gives for the world, written with LF line ends. The names are sorted in C-locale order. Each value is text: a date or a datetime in ISO 8601, any other value by as.character(). The order of the values within a name counts. Every element of the world counts, also an element that names no column of the table.

$dataset(name, world) regenerates a recipe with world. When the md5 of world equals world_md5, it checks the data against the recipe. It stops with an error that names the dataset when the row count differs from rows, or the md5 differs from md5. For any other world, the recipe is validated, its md5 is not checked, and a message says so. Two NULL worlds are equal. A recipe without rows has no row check.

Active bindings

name

The name of the table.

field_types

The field types of the table.

keys

The key columns of the table.

dir

The directory of the datasets, or NULL.

SyntheticTable$new()

Create a new SyntheticTable.

Usage

SyntheticTable$new(
  name,
  field_types,
  keys = NULL,
  validator_field_contents = validator_field_contents_blank,
  invariants = list(),
  profile = NULL,
  generator = NULL,
  dir = NULL
)

Arguments

name

The name of the table.

field_types

A named character vector of csdb field types.

keys

A character vector of key column names, or NULL.

validator_field_contents

A function of a data.table that returns TRUE for valid contents.

invariants

A named list of function(d) or function(d, world). Each returns TRUE, or a message that says why d fails.

profile

A csdb_profile, or NULL.

generator

A function(profile, n, seed, world) that returns a data.table, or NULL for simulate_from_profile().

dir

The directory of the datasets, or NULL for no datasets.

SyntheticTable$validate()

Check a data.table against the contract.

Usage

SyntheticTable$validate(d, world = NULL)

Arguments

d

A data.table.

world

NULL, or the list that each function(d, world) invariant receives.

Returns

d, invisibly. The method stops at the first check that fails, and the error names it.

SyntheticTable$random()

Generate and validate new data.

Usage

SyntheticTable$random(n = 1000L, seed = NULL, world = NULL)

Arguments

n

The number of rows, or NULL for the generator's own size.

seed

The seed. NULL draws a seed and reports it in a message, so you can replay a failure.

world

NULL, or a list that the generator receives.

Returns

A validated data.table.

SyntheticTable$dataset()

Get a fixed dataset by name.

Usage

SyntheticTable$dataset(name, world = NULL)

Arguments

name

The name of the dataset.

world

NULL, or a list that the generator receives. The md5 check runs only when the md5 of world equals the world_md5 of the recipe.

Returns

A validated data.table.

SyntheticTable$list_datasets()

List the fixed datasets.

Usage

SyntheticTable$list_datasets()

Returns

A data.table with name, kind (recipe or handmade), n, seed and description. A handmade dataset has NA in n, seed and description.

SyntheticTable$add_dataset()

Add a recipe, its row count and its md5 to datasets.yaml.

Usage

SyntheticTable$add_dataset(
  name,
  n,
  seed,
  description,
  overrides = list(),
  world = NULL
)

Arguments

name

The name of the dataset, lower snake case and new.

n

The number of rows, or NULL for the generator's own size.

seed

The seed.

description

One string that says what the dataset is for.

overrides

A named list that maps a column to one fixed value. The value replaces the column after generation.

world

NULL, or a list that the generator receives. The recipe stores its md5 as world_md5.

Returns

The validated data.table, invisibly.

SyntheticTable$check_hashes()

Regenerate each recipe that world made, and compare its row count and its md5.

Usage

SyntheticTable$check_hashes(world = NULL)

Arguments

world

NULL, or the world of the recipes to check.

Returns

A data.table with name and pass. pass is NA for a recipe that another world made.

SyntheticTable$clone()

The objects of this class are cloneable with this method.

Usage

SyntheticTable$clone(deep = FALSE)

Arguments

deep

Whether to make a deep clone.

Examples

st <- SyntheticTable$new(
  name = "people",
  field_types = c(id = "INTEGER", sex = "TEXT"),
  keys = "id",
  invariants = list(
    sex_known = function(d) if (all(!is.na(d$sex))) TRUE else "sex is missing."
  )
)
st$random(n = 5, seed = 1)
